title: NASA Saturn satellite sheet: Enceladus (II) mass 1.08×10^20 kg, radius 257 x 251 x 248 km
summary: The Saturn satellite fact sheet lists Enceladus (II) at mass 1.08 × 10^20 kg and radius 257 x 251 x 248 km.
body: NASA's Saturn satellite fact sheet lists Enceladus (II) with mass 1.08 × 10^20 kg, radius 257 x 251 x 248 km, mean density 1610 kg/m^3, and visual geometric albedo 1.0. Orbital parameters on the same sheet: Semi-major axis (10 3 km) = 238.02; Semi-major axis (Saturnian Radii) = 3.9494; Orbital Period* (days) = 1.370218; Rotation Period (days) = S; Inclination (degrees) = 0.00; Eccentricity = 0.0045. These are the cells printed on the sheet. The sheet does not say, on this row, which cells are a spacecraft measurement and which are an estimate. The sheet says R indicates retrograde motion, and S indicates synchronous rotation, the rotation period equal to the orbital period. Author of the sheet: Dr. David R. Williams, NASA Goddard Space Flight Center. Last Updated line: 22 July 2025.
